deep.reconstruction:
Page 0 of bundle 600_2 holds three separate notebook entries.

(1) Bernoulli function, a problem plus a sketch.
The task is: prove that the Bernoulli function phi(x) = B_p(x) is irreducible over Q. Here B_n(x) = sum_k C(n,k) B_k x^(n-k) is the Bernoulli polynomial, characterised by phi(x+1) - phi(x) = n x^(n-1). The sketch assumes the degree p is prime.

Step a, reduction mod p. For 0 < k < p, p divides C(p,k).
- By von Staudt–Clausen, the even-index B_k with k < p-1 have denominators prime to p. Odd B_k with k > 1 vanish. B_1 = -1/2 is p-integral for odd p.
- So all middle terms vanish mod p except the x-term C(p,p-1) B_{p-1} x = p B_{p-1} x.
- The constant term B_p is 0 for odd p.
- Hence phi(x) ≡ x^p + B~ x (mod p), with B~ := p B_{p-1}. (Identifying B~ as p B_{p-1} is my reading of the symbol.)

Step b, finding the coefficient. From the difference equation, phi(x+1) - phi(x) = p x^(p-1) ≡ 0, so phi(x+1) ≡ phi(x) (mod p). The machine reading 'phi(x)+1' should be phi(x+1).
- Substitute: (x+1)^p + B~(x+1) ≡ x^p + 1 + B~ x + B~.
- Comparing with x^p + B~ x gives 1 + B~ ≡ 0, i.e. B~ = p B_{p-1} ≡ -1 (mod p).
- This rederives the p-part of von Staudt–Clausen, given p-integrality of p B_{p-1}.

Step c, consequences. phi(x) ≡ x^p - x (mod p).
- Its roots mod p are 0, 1, ..., p-1, all distinct.
- Its discriminant is a unit mod p. Hilbert says it is ≡ 1; correctly it is ≡ (-1)^((p+1)/2), but in any case it is nonzero mod p.
- Hence disc B_p ≠ 0 over Q: B_p(x) is squarefree.
- That is where the note stops. Irreducibility itself is not derived.

(2) Probability, a philosophical remark. To construct an ideal probability apparatus (a wheel of fortune) would mean finding a natural phenomenon governed by no natural law, which contradicts our thinking.

(3) Theory of calculation, start of a programme continued on the next page. Set up a theory of reckoning: find out what the advantage of known arithmetic formulas consists in, and how to estimate it quantitatively. On the next page this becomes counting elementary operations as units, e.g. the cost of the n-th decimal digit of pi, or the fastest way to compute n!.
errors: The statement to be proved is false as stated for the ordinary Bernoulli polynomials of odd prime degree. For odd n >= 3, B_n(x) vanishes at 0, 1/2 and 1, so x(x-1/2)(x-1) divides it; e.g. B_3(x) = x(x-1/2)(x-1). At best the reduced polynomial B_p(x)/(x(x-1/2)(x-1)) could be irreducible, unless 'Bernoullische Function' means something else.
The argument proves only that B_p has distinct roots (nonzero discriminant), not irreducibility. Moreover x^p - x splits completely mod p, which gives no obstruction to factoring over Q.
Discriminant claim: disc(x^p - x) ≡ (-1)^((p+1)/2) mod p, not always 1. For p = 5 it is -256 ≡ -1. The conclusion that it is nonzero is still right.

Implicit steps not stated: p must be odd (for p = 2, B_2(x) = x^2 - x + 1/6 is not 2-integral). The reduction phi ≡ x^p + B~ x also tacitly uses von Staudt–Clausen information on the denominators of B_k for k < p-1, and the p-integrality of p B_{p-1}.

results.what: B_p(x) ≡ x^p - x (mod p) for odd prime p, with p B_{p-1} ≡ -1 (mod p) obtained from phi(x+1) ≡ phi(x)
results.modern_name: Reduction of Bernoulli polynomials mod p; part of the von Staudt–Clausen theorem
results.usually_credited_to: von Staudt and Clausen (1840); the polynomial congruences are classical (Carlitz and others)

results.what: Discriminant of B_p is nonzero (B_p squarefree), via the discriminant of x^p - x mod p
results.modern_name: Separability of Bernoulli polynomials; Brillhart showed Bernoulli polynomials have no multiple roots
results.usually_credited_to: Brillhart (1969); irreducibility questions also studied by Carlitz (1950s) and Inkeri (1959)

results.what: Problem of proving irreducibility of Bernoulli polynomials
results.modern_name: Irreducibility of Bernoulli polynomials (open in general; for odd n after removing trivial factors)

results.what: Programme of measuring computational cost by counting elementary operations (begins here, continued on the next page)
results.usually_credited_to: 20th century (Ostrowski 1954, Turing, Hartmanis–Stearns 1965); earlier remarks by Babbage and Lamé

deep.surprise_reason: The Bernoulli-polynomial entry is a routine (and incomplete, partly misdirected) exercise using von Staudt–Clausen. What is mildly notable is the early interest in irreducibility of Bernoulli polynomials. More so is the programme, started here, of a quantitative 'theory of calculation' counting elementary operations, a proto-complexity idea. Hilbert's general interest in such questions is not unknown, and the entry is only a sketch.
